title: The Longest Day
checkpoint: Year 1 Summer 2, week 4 — School readiness — Phase 6: new sounds -er, -est
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 6 book for the endings '-er' and '-est'. Point out that the root word stays the same and only the ending changes: long, longer, longest. Ask your child to find all three on the last page.

pages.text: It was the longest day of the year. The sun got up first, and then the birds did.
pages.illustration: Very early summer morning. The sun already high over the garden while Pip is still asleep in the ivy nest, one eye squinting open in disbelief. Long shadows the wrong way round. Pale washed-out gold.

pages.text: "I am the fastest," said Ned. "I am faster than a frog and faster than a fish."
pages.illustration: Ned the gold duckling standing on the pond edge in a running pose, chest out, utterly convinced of himself. A frog and a fish in the water beside him looking distinctly unimpressed.

pages.text: "You are not," said Pip. "But you are the loudest. You are much louder than me."
pages.illustration: Pip perched on a stone with both wings clamped over where his ears would be. Ned mid-quack, beak wide, drawn slightly bigger than life. Comic size contrast.

pages.text: Moss was not fast at all. He was the softest and the roundest of all three.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog ambling along a garden path with a leaf on his back, taking his time. Pip and Ned already tiny in the distance ahead. Warm and completely unhurried.

pages.text: "I am the smallest," said Pip, "but I can get to the highest branch on the oak."
pages.illustration: Looking straight up the old oak. Pip a small speck near the very top, wings out. The trunk enormous below him. Vertical composition to sell the height.

pages.text: Ned tried. He got to a small branch, and then a smaller one, and then the grass.
pages.illustration: Three-step sequence across the page: Ned scrambling onto a low branch, Ned slipping to a lower one, Ned sitting in the grass with a leaf on his head. Same pose, three stages. Very funny.

pages.text: The day got hotter. Then the shade under the big oak was the best spot in the garden.
pages.illustration: All three squashed together in a strip of deep cool shadow under the hedge, panting slightly. The rest of the page bleached bright with heat. Strong light-dark contrast.

pages.text: “The longest day,” said Moss, “and I think this is the longest nap.”
pages.illustration: Moss curled into a ball, fast asleep; Pip asleep on top of him; Ned asleep upside down with his feet in the air. Late evening light, still not dark. Peaceful and silly.
